## anu-p08 — C1

**SUMMARY.** What true, untrue, little-much, eternal, not eternal, Māyā-stained, self-pure — all shines unsorted in the consciousness-mirror. Known as rising from own-grasping consciousness, this is own-experience-risen glory: Lordhood — worship.

*Rasa: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta (wonder) — The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of Lordhood (viśveśvaratva); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at all opposites shining in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness. The rasa is the tranquility of Lordhood — the hymn that began in anupāya ends in worship.*
